title: Flow Off Main Thread Node Computation With Loading Chrome
description:
Node computation in the flow graph (flow_core FlowHost::evaluate_internal / touch_channel_eval) runs synchronously on whatever thread mutates the host. The React renderer's FlowGraphCanvasHost owns a main-thread FlowSession and calls loadFixtureJson/evaluateSync directly, so heavy evaluations (e.g. procedural-3d's "Sphere Cut With Torus" example, which drives brep.bool.cut -> boolean_mesh_sync, a ~20s WASM stall) freeze the UI. The procedural plugin worker also re-evaluates the whole graph synchronously on every action/render.

Goal: move all flow node computation off the main thread and show per-node loading chrome (the dag canvas already has unfed animated active/stale border chrome) while nodes compute. Verify on procedural-3d "Sphere Cut With Torus".

Approach (see approved plan): tick-driven evaluation inside the plugin worker via a budgeted evaluator (neural/engine), a shared FlowEvalDriver (flow/core), pending_effects wired through refreshUi/action responses using the existing HostEffect::DispatchAction self-dispatch loop, new NodeGraphScene.evalJson / World3dScene.statusJson fields, and renderer changes (React + wgpu) that stop evaluating locally and instead apply eval outputs + computing progress from the scene.

Full plan on disk at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/flow-the-computation-of-sparkling-whale.md.
summary:
Moved flow node evaluation off the main thread end-to-end and wired up per-node loading chrome, per the approved plan.

**Root fix**: `flow/core` no longer auto-evaluates on any mutation — removed `touch_channel_eval` (~28 call sites) plus three previously-unnoticed hidden `self.evaluate()` calls inside `set_slider_value`/`set_note_text`/`set_image_src` (these were the actual cause of a live slider drag re-running the whole graph on every pointer-move tick). Added `neural_engine::evaluate_channels_budgeted` (stops after N cache-missed dispatches, returns the not-yet-computed ids) and `flow_core`'s `FlowEvalDriver`, which ticks one node at a time via `HostEffect::DispatchAction("flowEvalTick")` and reports `computingJson`/`evalJson`. `DocumentApp::pending_effects` (new, default no-op) is the chokepoint — called once per `refreshUi` pass (before rendering, so the same pass sees fresh computing state) — so any mutation path re-arms the chain without each action needing its own check.

Procedural plugin (2D+3D) and the flow plugin now drive this: renders never evaluate (stale/placeholder meshes shown while computing), `evaluated_preview_payload`'s `host.evaluate()` stays but only runs post-convergence where it's a cheap all-cache-hit walk against the shared `NeuralCache`. React renderer's canvas session stopped evaluating locally (`commitFixture` no longer calls the removed `evaluateSync`) and now applies `evalJson`/`computingJson` from the scene; `World3dHost` shows a spinner overlay when `statusJson` reports computing. wgpu renderer's `sync_flow_host` mirrors this (applies `eval_json` instead of evaluating).

**Verified** (isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` to dodge this session's extreme shared-lock contention — see updated `feedback-concurrent-cargo-workspace-churn` memory): `flow_core` 85/86, `neural_engine` 32/32, `flow-plugin` 23/23, `procedural-plugin` 42/43, `semio-framework-plugin` 91/91, `ui_wgpu` 17/17 — both remaining failures independently confirmed pre-existing/unrelated (zero diff, reproduce identically without any of this ticket's changes: one is a first-ever-eval dispatch-count assumption that predates this fixture's current shape, the other is a JSON-string-escaping check against a field that's always been double-encoded). TypeScript typechecks clean. Added/extended tests for the budgeted evaluator, the `FlowEvalDriver` state machine (incl. mid-chain coalescing), and procedural-3d's computing-chrome lifecycle on the "Sphere Cut With Torus" example — plus fixed 5 existing flow_core tests and 1 procedural-plugin test that asserted the old (now intentionally removed) auto-eval-on-mutation behavior.

Also fixed opportunistically (blocking, pre-existing, unrelated to this ticket): `procedural-plugin`'s `Cargo.toml` was missing a `ui_styling` dependency that code already referenced — any truly fresh build was already broken; the shared `target/` dir was masking it via stale cached artifacts.

Deferred to a follow-up (chip already spawned): wgpu-renderer parity for the `flowEvalTick` self-dispatch loop and the computing-status badge (React renderer has both; wgpu only got the minimal `sync_flow_host` fix).

Files: flow/core/rs/lib.rs, neural/engine/rs/lib.rs, flow/plugin/rs/lib.rs, procedural/plugin/rs/lib.rs, procedural/plugin/rs/Cargo.toml, framework/plugin/rs/lib.rs, framework/core/js/index.ts, framework/renderer/react/index.tsx, framework/renderer/wgpu/rs/lib.rs, ui/wgpu/rs/lib.rs, infinite/world/rs/lib.rs.
